1: Chapter 1: A Guest on a Rainy Night
It had been raining in Doldari village for three days. Kim Haneul’s older sister had left for Seoul in the spring, and since then Haneul had been running the village’s small apothecary on her own.
As night fell, she closed the outer door, counted the day’s earnings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when an urgent knocking came from downstairs, followed by a man’s voice. “Is anyone there?”
A young man stood at the door, soaked to the skin. The cloth wrapped around his left arm was stained with blood. He introduced himself as Park Junho and said he was with the Azure Dragon Society.
“Please treat my wound,” Park Junho said in a low voice. “I’ll pay you. Will three thousand five hundred nyang be enough?”
He drew a letter wrapped in oiled paper from inside his coat. “This letter must be delivered to Cheongpungsa by the eighteenth of May.”
Haneul thought to herself. The neighbors were already green with envy over how well the apothecary was doing, and now a strange man had turned up in the middle of the night.
Still, Haneul refused the money and simply said, “I’ll guide you to the mountain early tomorrow morning.”
2: At daybreak the two set out. Haneul carried a basket on her back; inside were fistfuls of rice, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

On the mountainside they met old Lee Youngsoo, who was chopping firewood. He set down his axe and lowered his voice. Last evening, he said, three strangers had been asking about a wounded young man at the edge of the village.
"Haneul, take the side path," Lee Youngsoo said. "The main road is dangerous." Haneul thanked the old man.
The side path was narrow and slippery. Haneul led the way, planting each step firmly. Park Junho followed in silence.
By noon the rain had stopped and the mountain mist slowly lifted; in the distance the roof of Cheongpungsa came into view. A nun stood at the temple gate. It was Jeonghye, who received guests.
Jeonghye took the letter, checked the red seal on the envelope, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting for this letter for two years."
Park Junho said to Haneul, "You are my savior." Haneul smiled and replied, "Then next time you come, fix the roof of the medicine shop." Park Junho stayed at the temple.
That evening Haneul came down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already dark. She lit the lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
